mergedParams.userDescription: Stretchy or 'jiggly' text animation on interaction.

output.title: Jiggly Stretchy Text Animation on Hover/Click

prompts.prompt: Create a typography preset that simulates elastic jello-like physics when text appears or interacts. Think of it like a video editor adding a 'wiggle' expression in After Effects - the text should stretch vertically when it lands, compress slightly, then oscillate back to normal with decreasing amplitude over 800-1200ms. The animation should feel organic and playful, like dropping jello onto a surface. Use a BaseLayout container with 'relative' positioning and apply the jiggly effect to individual TextAtom components for each word. The stretch should primarily affect scaleY (going from 0.7 to 1.3 to 0.9 to 1.05 to 1.0), while scaleX inversely compensates (1.3 to 0.8 to 1.1 to 0.95 to 1.0) to maintain volume consistency. Add a subtle rotation oscillation (-2deg to 2deg) synchronized with the stretch for extra personality. This mimics the 'overshoot' principle in animation where objects don't stop immediately but continue past their resting point before settling.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative flex items-center justify-center gap-2' containing individual TextAtom components per word. Effects: Use generic keyframe effects array with spring easing for natural physics. AnimationRange sequence: [0-15%: scaleY 0.7→1.3, scaleX 1.3→0.8], [15-30%: scaleY 1.3→0.9, scaleX 0.8→1.1], [30-45%: scaleY 0.9→1.05, scaleX 1.1→0.95], [45-60%: scaleY 1.05→1.0, scaleX 0.95→1.0]. Add rotate effect: [0-25%: 0→-2deg], [25-50%: -2deg→2deg], [50-75%: 2deg→-1deg], [75-100%: -1deg→0]. Use transform-origin: center bottom for grounded feel. Apply will-change: transform for GPU acceleration. Consider using internal effect preset for reusability across multiple text elements.

prompts.prompt: Design a rubber-band snap text animation preset where letters stretch horizontally before snapping back into place with kinetic energy. Picture editing a video where text gets pulled like taffy from one side, then releases with a satisfying elastic recoil. Each letter should have a staggered delay (50ms between letters) creating a wave effect across the text. The stretch phase should be slower (400ms with ease-out), building tension, then the snap-back should be rapid (200ms with a custom cubic-bezier for that rubber-band snap feel). Add a subtle blur during maximum stretch to simulate motion blur you'd add in video post-production. The text should also slightly overshoot its final position before settling, like a rubber band that's been released.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with containerProps.className='inline-flex items-baseline' containing TextAtom for each letter. Create custom effect with translateX and scaleX properties. Animation phases: [0-40%: translateX 0→-30px, scaleX 1→1.5, blur 0→2px with ease-out], [40-60%: translateX -30px→15px, scaleX 1.5→0.9, blur 2px→0 with cubic-bezier(0.68,-0.55,0.265,1.55)], [60-80%: translateX 15px→-5px, scaleX 0.9→1.05], [80-100%: translateX -5px→0, scaleX 1.05→1]. Use childrenProps with staggered relative timing (delay: index * 0.05). Apply pointer-events: none during animation. Consider using repeatChildrenProps for consistent letter behavior.

prompts.prompt: Build a bouncy gelatin text preset where words wobble like they're made of soft jelly when they appear. Imagine keyframing a 3D jelly simulation in video editing software - the text should deform asymmetrically with different parts moving at slightly different rates. Use skew transformations combined with scale to create the wobbly effect. The animation should have multiple oscillation cycles with decreasing intensity, simulating damped harmonic motion. Add a subtle color shift during wobbles (slight hue rotation) to enhance the jelly-like quality. This creates the illusion of translucent, refractive material catching light differently as it moves.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout container with TextAtom components. Use transform matrix for complex deformations: combine scaleX, scaleY, skewX, skewY. Animation timeline with spring easing: [0-10%: scale(1,0.6) skew(5deg,-3deg)], [10-25%: scale(0.9,1.2) skew(-8deg,4deg)], [25-40%: scale(1.1,0.95) skew(3deg,-2deg)], [40-55%: scale(0.98,1.03) skew(-2deg,1deg)], [55-70%: scale(1.01,0.99) skew(1deg,0deg)], [70-100%: scale(1,1) skew(0deg,0deg)]. Add filter effect for hue-rotate: oscillate between -5deg and 5deg synchronized with wobble. Use containerProps.style for transform-style: preserve-3d. Duration: 1200ms total. Consider internal effect preset named 'jelly-wobble' for reuse.

prompts.prompt: Create a liquid morph text animation where letters behave like viscous fluid drops that merge and separate. Think of it as applying a liquify effect in video editing - text should appear to melt slightly, ripple, then solidify. Use CSS clip-path with animated polygon points to create organic, flowing shapes around the text. The animation should include a 'surface tension' effect where the text bulges outward before contracting. Add multiple layers of animation: the main morph, a secondary ripple effect using box-shadow animations, and a subtle transparency fluctuation to simulate depth. This mimics advanced compositing techniques where multiple effects layers create complex motion.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative overflow-hidden'. TextAtom wrapped in div with animated clip-path using polygon. Keyframe sequence: [0%: clip-path: polygon with standard rectangle], [25%: bulging polygon with curved edges], [50%: contracted wavy shape], [75%: expanding ripple shape], [100%: return to rectangle]. Combine with scale animation: [0-30%: scale 0.8→1.1], [30-60%: scale 1.1→0.95], [60-100%: scale 0.95→1]. Add box-shadow animation for ripples: animate from 0 to 20px blur with rgba(0,0,0,0.2). Opacity effect: [0-20%: 0.7→1], [20-40%: 1→0.9], [40-100%: 0.9→1]. Use will-change: clip-path, transform, opacity. Duration: 1000ms with ease-in-out.

prompts.prompt: Develop a spring-loaded compression text effect where text squashes down like a spring being compressed, then bounces up with stored energy. Visualize this as adding a 'squash and stretch' animation in a video timeline - the text should compress to 40% height while expanding width to 160% to maintain volume, then spring back overshooting to 120% height before settling. Include secondary motion where individual letters rotate slightly during compression (like springs twisting under pressure). Add particle effects using pseudo-elements that 'pop' out during the spring release for extra dynamism. This emulates particle systems often used in motion graphics to enhance impact.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with TextAtom components. Primary effect: scaleY animation [0-20%: 1→0.4], [20-40%: 0.4→1.2], [40-60%: 1.2→0.9], [60-80%: 0.9→1.05], [80-100%: 1.05→1]. Inverse scaleX: [0-20%: 1→1.6], [20-40%: 1.6→0.85], [40-60%: 0.85→1.1], [60-80%: 1.1→0.97], [80-100%: 0.97→1]. Add rotate effect with slight random variation per letter using childrenProps. For particles: use ::before and ::after pseudo-elements with position: absolute, animate opacity and transform: translate() scale() for burst effect. Transform-origin: bottom center for grounded compression. Use cubic-bezier(0.175, 0.885, 0.32, 1.275) for bounce easing.

prompts.prompt: Design an accordion-style stretch text animation where text expands and contracts horizontally like an accordion being played. Picture time-remapping footage of an accordion - the text should stretch wide with decreasing letter-spacing, then compress with overlapping letters, creating a rhythmic pulse. Include alternating vertical displacement for odd/even letters (like accordion keys moving). Add a subtle 3D perspective tilt during maximum stretch to enhance depth perception. The animation should have musical timing with consistent rhythm, making it perfect for music-synchronized content. Include gradient color transitions that flow across letters during the stretch cycle.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='inline-flex perspective-1000'. Individual TextAtom per letter with alternating translateY for odd/even indices. Letter-spacing animation: [0-25%: 0→20px], [25-50%: 20px→-5px], [50-75%: -5px→10px], [75-100%: 10px→0]. ScaleX per letter: [0-25%: 1→0.7], [25-50%: 0.7→1.3], [50-75%: 1.3→0.85], [75-100%: 0.85→1]. Odd letters: translateY oscillates 0→10px→0, even letters: 0→-10px→0. Add rotateY: [0-50%: 0→5deg], [50-100%: 5deg→0] for perspective. Background gradient animation using linear-gradient with animated color stops. Duration: 800ms with ease-in-out. Consider using waveform effects if audio source available.

prompts.prompt: Create a magnetic repulsion text effect where letters push away from each other when appearing, then snap back together with magnetic attraction. Think of this as simulating physics in After Effects - each letter has a 'force field' that initially repels neighbors, causing them to spread apart with elastic tension, then they're pulled back together overshooting slightly before settling. Add rotational torque where letters spin based on their position relative to center (outer letters rotate more). Include a subtle electric glow effect during maximum repulsion to visualize the 'magnetic field'. This recreates advanced expression-driven animations commonly used in kinetic typography.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with position: relative, TextAtom components with position: absolute for precise control. Calculate translateX based on letter index from center: center letters move less, edge letters move more. Animation: [0-30%: translateX from 0 to calculated spread position (index-center)*30px], [30-60%: snap back to (index-center)*-10px overshoot], [60-100%: settle to 0]. Rotation based on position: rotate: (index-center)*15deg at peak, settling to 0. Add glow using text-shadow: animate from none to '0 0 20px rgba(100,200,255,0.8)' at peak repulsion. Use spring physics easing: cubic-bezier(0.68,-0.55,0.265,1.55). Duration: 1200ms. Consider using internal effect preset for magnetic physics reusability.

prompts.prompt: Build a taffy-pull text animation where text stretches vertically like pulled candy, becoming thinner in the middle while maintaining thick ends. Imagine using mesh warp in video editing - the text should deform non-uniformly with the center stretching more than edges. Create multiple stretch points that pull at different rates, simulating hands pulling taffy. Add a twisting motion during stretch for that characteristic taffy spiral. Include subtle color banding that appears during maximum stretch (like stretched candy showing layers). The snap-back should be elastic with multiple diminishing oscillations.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container, TextAtom with SVG filter for non-uniform distortion. Use feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap for organic stretch. Combine with CSS transforms: scaleY animates [0-35%: 1→2.5 ease-out], [35-50%: 2.5→0.7 ease-in], [50-65%: 0.7→1.2], [65-80%: 1.2→0.95], [80-100%: 0.95→1]. ScaleX inverse compensation. Add rotate for twist: [0-35%: 0→180deg], [35-100%: 180deg→0]. For color banding: use repeating-linear-gradient with animated background-size. Text-fill-color: transparent, background-clip: text for gradient effect. Filter baseFrequency animates for distortion intensity. Duration: 1500ms for smooth taffy effect.

prompts.prompt: Design a bubble-gum pop text effect where letters inflate like bubble gum, stretch to breaking point, then pop back to normal size. Picture slow-motion footage of bubble gum - text should expand uniformly at first, then develop a bulge that grows asymmetrically before 'popping'. Include a brief moment where text becomes semi-transparent at maximum stretch (like thin bubble gum). Add subtle surface highlights that move across the text during inflation to simulate the shiny bubble surface. The pop should be sudden with a brief scale overshoot and vibration. Include optional particle burst on pop for dramatic effect.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with TextAtom components. Multi-phase animation: [0-40%: uniform scale 1→1.8 with ease-out], [40-70%: asymmetric bulge using scaleX 1.8→2.2, scaleY 1.8→2.5], [70-75%: hold at maximum], [75-80%: rapid pop to scale 0.9], [80-90%: overshoot to 1.15], [90-100%: settle to 1 with vibration]. Opacity: [60-70%: 1→0.6], [75-80%: 0.6→1]. Add moving highlight using linear-gradient animated via background-position. For pop particles: create multiple absolutely positioned divs animated with random trajectories. Use filter: blur() slightly at maximum stretch. Transform-origin: center for uniform expansion. Duration: 2000ms total with custom easing per phase.

prompts.prompt: Create a slinky-spring text animation where text compresses and extends like a slinky toy going down stairs. Visualize stop-motion animation of a slinky - text should compress at top, extend downward with momentum, compress at bottom, then spring back up. Each letter should have a slight delay creating a wave propagation effect. Include rotational oscillation that follows the spring motion (letters tilt forward when extending, backward when compressing). Add metallic sheen effect using animated gradients to enhance the spring coil appearance. The motion should feel heavy and momentum-driven, not just elastic.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='flex items-end gap-1'. TextAtom per letter with staggered timing via childrenProps (delay: index*0.08). Primary animation: translateY [0-20%: 0→-20px compress], [20-50%: -20px→40px extend with acceleration], [50-70%: 40px→-10px rebound], [70-85%: -10px→5px], [85-100%: 5px→0]. ScaleY: [0-20%: 1→0.7], [20-50%: 0.7→1.3], [50-70%: 1.3→0.9], [70-100%: 0.9→1]. RotateX: [0-20%: 0→-10deg], [20-50%: -10deg→15deg], [50-70%: 15deg→-5deg], [70-100%: -5deg→0]. Add metallic gradient using linear-gradient with animated angle. Use physics-based easing: cubic-bezier(0.45, 0.05, 0.55, 0.95) for momentum feel. Duration: 1800ms per cycle.
